First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
		13 &= \dfrac{6y+8}{2} \
		2 \cdot 13 &= 2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{2}\right)  \   
		2 \cdot 13 &= \cancel{2} \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{\cancel{2}}\right) \   
		26 &= 6y+8
	}
$$

Next, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\eqalign{
		26 &= 6y+8 \
		26-8 &= 6y+8-8 \
		18 &= 6y \
		\dfrac{18}{6} &= \dfrac{6y}{6} \
		3 &= y
	}
$$

Thus, $y=3.$
